words.enExample: All employees must abide by the company's code of conduct.
words.zhExample: 所有员工都必须遵守公司的行为准则。
words.note: 💡 abide 本身是「忍受、停留」，正式用语。常用于规章文书：abide by the rules / abide by the decision。口语里更常说 comply with 或 follow。

words.enExample: Approval from legal is the bottleneck in this process.
words.zhExample: 法务审批是这个流程里的瓶颈。
words.note: 💡 形象词：瓶口细，液体流得慢。搭配 identify/remove a bottleneck。复盘会常用句式：The main bottleneck is…（主要卡点是…）。

words.enExample: Open offices are not always conducive to deep work.
words.zhExample: 开放式办公室并不总利于深度工作。
words.note: 💡 永远搭配 to：be conducive to sth/doing sth（to 是介词，后接动名词）。写作替换 good for 的高级表达，六级和雅思写作都很吃香。

words.enExample: The bonus scheme spurred sales across all regions.
words.zhExample: 奖金制度刺激了各地区的销售。
words.note: 💡 原指「马刺」，引申为鞭策。名词用法也很常见：a spur to innovation。句型 spur sb to do sth / spur growth，商务报道高频动词。

words.enExample: The turnout at the town hall meeting was impressive.
words.zhExample: 员工大会的到场人数相当可观。
words.note: 💡 turn out（结果如何）派生的名词。常见 a high/low turnout。活动策划复盘必用：We had a great turnout.（来了很多人。）注意别写成 turn out。

essay.title: The Harvest of Small Attention
essay.author: 佚名
paragraphs: We imagine a harvest as an event: one loud week, carts in the field, everything finished at once. But the yield depended entirely on thousands of unrecorded mornings — weeding, watching, waiting in the right order. The same is true of attention. Nothing gathered suddenly was gathered suddenly. The ordinary days simply did their work and stayed quiet about it.

Most days offer us perhaps two or three things worth noticing, and we walk past nearly all of them because they are unimpressive. A neighbour's hedge that has grown since August. The way a colleague pauses before answering. To discern the valuable from the merely visible takes practice, and the price of skipping it is that everything becomes one long blur we overlook entirely.

An attentive person is not a busy one. Attention is not speed; it is willingness to dwell. My grandfather could stand in front of a single apple tree for ten minutes, doing nothing that anyone would pay for, and come away knowing things. He was not smarter than me. He simply was not in a hurry to leave.

There is an old word for this kind of work. To glean is to walk behind the reapers and gather what they have left — the small overlooked portion that belongs to whoever cares to stoop for it. Nobody makes a living that way. But you can make a life. What you reap from such hours is not money, and it does not spoil.

I am trying, these autumn mornings, to go more slowly through the first hour. To look at the light on the wall before I look at the screen. To finish one thing before beginning another. It feels wasteful and a little pointless. Then the month ends, and I find I have something to show for it: a quiet harvest, gathered slowly.
translations: 我们总把收成想象成一件大事：热闹的一周，田里的马车，一切同时结束。然而那份产量，完全取决于几千个无人记录的早晨——除草、观察、按正确的顺序等待。留意这件事也是如此。没有什么是突然聚拢起来的，从来都是寻常日子默默做完自己的工作，然后对此保持沉默。
大多数日子大概会奉上两三件值得留意的事，而我们几乎全都走过去了，因为它们不起眼。邻居家的树篱自八月起长高了一截。同事答话前的那一顿。从仅仅可见之物中认出有价值的那部分，需要练习；而跳过这一步的代价，是一切都变成一团长长的模糊，被我们彻底忽略。
一个留心的人，并不是一个忙碌的人。留意不是速度，而是愿意停留。我的外祖父能在一棵苹果树前站上十分钟，做着任何人都不会付钱的事，然后带着某些了解离开。他并不比我聪明。他只是不急着离场。
这类劳作有个古老的词。拾穗，就是走在收割者身后，捡起他们落下的东西——那小小一撮被人忽略的部分，归任何愿意弯腰的人所有。没有人靠这个谋生。但你却可以靠它过一种生活。从这样的时光里收割到的不是钱，也不会腐坏。
这些秋天的早晨，我在试着把第一个小时过得更慢一些。先看墙上的光，再看屏幕。先做完一件事，再开始另一件。这感觉有些浪费，也有点没用。然后这个月末了，我发现自己终于有了可以交出的东西：一份安静的收成，慢慢地聚拢起来的。

grammar.point: 破折号引出的补充说明（同位成分）
grammar.example: "But the yield depended entirely on thousands of unrecorded mornings — weeding, watching, waiting in the right order."
grammar.note: 破折号后可接一组并列成分，对前面的名词作具体说明，作用介于同位语与插入语之间；三个动名词连用形成排比节奏。 举一反三：举一反三：One habit saved her — rising early, writing first, worrying later. / 一个习惯救了她——早起，先写，后愁。

grammar.point: worth + 动名词（主动形式表被动）
grammar.example: "Most days offer us perhaps two or three things worth noticing."
grammar.note: be worth doing 中的 doing 用主动形式却表被动含义，不可用被动语态；worth 前常用 well 修饰。 举一反三：举一反三：That old lane is well worth walking twice. / 那条老路很值得走两遍。

grammar.point: try to do 与 try doing
grammar.example: "I am trying, these autumn mornings, to go more slowly through the first hour."
grammar.note: try to do 表示设法去做某件困难的事，强调努力；try doing 表示试着做某事以观效果，强调试验。 举一反三：举一反三：Try keeping the phone in another room for one evening. / 试着把手机放在别的房间一晚看看。

vocab.enExample: The harvest depended on a thousand mornings nobody wrote down.
vocab.zhExample: 收成取决于一千个无人记录的早晨。
vocab.note: 用法：a good harvest；harvest the field

vocab.enExample: She gleaned what facts she could from a very short letter.
vocab.zhExample: 她从一封很短的信里尽力拾取能用的信息。
vocab.note: 用法：glean sth from sth；glean a few facts

vocab.enExample: An attentive listener is rarer than a clever talker.
vocab.zhExample: 留心的倾听者比聪明的说话者更少见。
vocab.note: 用法：attentive to detail；an attentive listener

vocab.enExample: Do not overlook the small changes; they arrive first.
vocab.zhExample: 不要忽略那些细微的变化，它们总是先到。

vocab.enExample: Attention is not speed; it is willingness to dwell.
vocab.zhExample: 留意不是速度，而是愿意停留。
vocab.note: 用法：dwell on sth；dwell in a place

vocab.enExample: The ordinary days simply did their work and stayed quiet.
vocab.zhExample: 寻常的日子只是做完自己的事，然后保持沉默。
vocab.note: 用法：an ordinary day；out of the ordinary

vocab.enExample: You reap in November what September planted.
vocab.zhExample: 九月种下的，十一月收获。
vocab.note: 用法：reap the benefit/reward；reap what you sow

vocab.enExample: To discern the valuable from the merely visible takes practice.
vocab.zhExample: 从仅仅可见之物中分辨出有价值的，需要练习。
vocab.note: 用法：discern sth from sth；discern a pattern
